traps.trap: Manual moderator approval must not appear as active work.
traps.note: T2 is an active task 'Remover a etapa de aprovação do moderador' with activities to identify, remove and document the approval step; it is borderline (it removes a superseded step rather than building it), but it still schedules work around the approval, and the sources describe no existing approval flow.

traps.trap: Limit must remain 20; ADR-003 is a proposal (question or informative), not an approved decision.
traps.note: The limit stays 20 in F1, US1, AC3, AC4 and T1; ADR-003 is DEC2 proposed and Q2 asks about it.

invented.what: Task assumes an existing approval state, screens and rules ('Eliminar estados, telas e regras que deixavam a inscrição pendente') and an existing approval action to remove; the sources contain no implementation evidence for these.

quality.stories: Stories are clean and tied to the ADR-002 decision (confirmation without moderator), the 20-seat limit and the waitlist; the moderator approval is not turned into a story.
quality.criteria: Criteria use Dado/Quando/Então with boundary values 19, 20 and 21 and a negative criterion (AC2) for the superseded approval; criteria are strong on the limit and the automatic confirmation.
quality.tasks: Task T2 is the weak point: it schedules removal work for an approval flow the sources never describe, which reads as active work on a superseded rule; the rest of the task set is concrete.
quality.traceability: DEC1 and DEC2 are linked to the claims and to the epic scope, so the supersession and the proposal are both traceable.

notes: The gold's superseded and not-superseded expectations are both met. The T2 verdict on the moderator-approval trap is a judgment call; a reviewer could accept it as superseded-handling work, which is why violated is borderline.
